food.name: Western-style restaurant in Azumino

sights.name: Omi Village Butai Sakura
sights.name_en: Butai-zakura at former Zagoto Elementary Butai schoolhouse (built Meiji 7): a rare half-double weeping higan cherry about 350 years old.
sights.description: Cherry tree about 350 years old, a rare semi-double weeping red higan type whose petal count varies by bloom, before the Meiji 7 former Zakoji Elementary stage schoolhouse, lit at night.

sights.name: Toyama Sakura Kawazu Sakura
sights.name_en: Toyama-go cherry plantings: about 60-70 Somei-yoshino along 2.5 km of the Toyama River left bank, plus early Kawazu and weeping cherries on the right.
sights.description: Cherry blossom viewing spot in Iida.

sights.name: Ho Hisashi Tera no Shakunage (Shakunage)
sights.name_en: Hojuji Temple rhododendrons on a terrace overlooking the Tenryu River; bloom typically late April to mid-May.
sights.description: Rhododendrons in the natural garden of a Zen temple on a rise overlooking the Tenryu River, in season from late April to mid-May.

sights.name: no Soko Yama Forest Park
sights.name_en: Nosokoyama Forest Park with cherry blossoms in spring, maple color in autumn, playgrounds, and camping facilities.
sights.description: Forest park with cherry blossoms in spring, maple leaves in autumn, playground equipment, and camping facilities.

sights.name: Myo Kon Park
sights.name_en: Myokin Park for mallet golf, cycling, nearby amago fishing on the Matsukawa, camping, azaleas, and autumn color.
sights.description: Park with mallet golf, cycling, a campground, and amago fishing in the nearby Matsukawa, plus spring azaleas and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Mitsuishi no Shidarezakura
sights.name_en: Weeping cherry by the Sanseki stones on the old Akiba road in Shimohisakata; about 300 years old and 15 m tall.
sights.description: Weeping cherry, estimated 300 years old and 15 meters tall, planted beside the Mitsuishi rocks along the old Akiba road; nearby potholes are a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Sakuramaru no Fufu Sakura
sights.name_en: Meoto-zakura at former Iida Castle Sakuramaru: a weeping cherry and Edohigan said to be about 400 years old and roughly 20 m tall.
sights.description: Weeping cherry and Edohigan cherry trees bloom leaning together at the former Iida Castle Sakuramaru palace, about 20 m tall with trunks about 10 m in girth and an estimated age of 400 years.

sights.name: Kiyohide Sakura
sights.name_en: Seishu-zakura, an Edohigan at Atago Shrine traditionally planted in 1240; Iida oldest cherry and a city natural monument.
sights.description: Edohigan cherry at Atago Shrine, said to have been planted by Hoin Kiyohide in 1240, designated an Iida City natural monument and estimated over 760 years old, with night illumination.

sights.name: Omiya Tori no Sakura Namiki
sights.name_en: About 700 m of cherry trees (about 150, mainly Somei-yoshino) from Omiya Shrine toward Apple Avenue, with blossom festivals and night lighting.
sights.description: Cherry avenue of about 150 trees, mainly Somei-yoshino and higan cherry, running about 700 m from Omiya Shrine, with a blossom tunnel, festival, and night lighting when in bloom.

sights.name: Sen Sho Tera no Shidarezakura
sights.name_en: Weeping cherry over 400 years old in front of Senshoji main hall, with night lighting during bloom.
sights.description: A weeping cherry more than 400 years old stands in front of Senshoji Temple's main hall, with a gentle-faced Buddha statue beneath it and night illumination.

sights.name: Yasutomi Cherry Tree
sights.description: Prefectural natural monument Edohigan cherry at Iida City Art Museum, estimated 450 years old and 20 meters tall.

sights.name: Hinatsu Konosuke Memorial Museum
sights.description: Modeled on Iida-born writer Hinatsu Konosuke's later home, it displays his books, letters, and belongings.

sights.name: Iida City Archaeological Museum
sights.description: Displays pre-pottery artifacts from Chuo Expressway excavations and stands beside Kaizenji Temple.

sights.name: Iida City Kawamoto Kihachiro Puppet Art Museum
sights.description: Art museum of puppet artist Kawamoto Kihachiro, showing over 100 puppets from NHK dramas, animation, and commercials.

sights.name: Tenryukyo Autumn Foliage
sights.description: Where the Tenryu River is narrowest, Tenryukyo's autumn colors peak from early to mid-November.

sights.name: Kunio Yanagita Museum
sights.description: This relocated 1927 Tokyo study of folklore pioneer Kunio Yanagita displays his books and Iida connections.

sights.name: Shusui Beauty Painting Museum
sights.description: Active nihonga painter Shusui, pupil of the late Ito Tansui, permanently exhibits his beauty paintings.

sights.name: Kannon Reisui Spring
sights.description: This drinkable Ryuenji spring, long used as household water, is very high in calcium and magnesium.

sights.name: Ryuenji Temple
sights.description: Toyama clan graves lie beneath old cedars, and Kannon Reisui spring rises within the temple grounds.

sights.name: Yanagishima Checkpoint Site
sights.description: Toyama Tosa-no-kami built it on Ieyasu's orders to police Osaka fugitives and control timber.

sights.name: Former Zakouji Omi School Building

sights.name: Imada Puppets
sights.description: Puppetry began in 1704 to enliven the Omiya Hachiman Shrine festival and is dedicated there each October.

sights.name: Kudagayu Ritual
sights.description: Held at Nakago Hachiman Shrine to divine that year's crop harvest.

sights.name: Hokuryu Mizumi no Na no Hana

sights.description: Ryukinka flowers at Numanohara Marsh on the Madarao Highlands, blooming after skunk cabbage as snow melts, usually viewed from early to late May.

sights.name: Madarao Highlands no Mizubasho
sights.description: Colony of Asian skunk cabbage at Numanohara wetland, seen as the snow melts, with a usual peak from late April to mid-May.

sights.name: Nishi Otaki Dam Cherry Blossoms

sights.name: Nagamine Supotsu Park Cherry Blossoms

sights.description: Alpine lake 13.3 m deep, called goshinsui, about 2.5 hours from the Ontake ropeway end and 1 hour from the summit.

sights.name: Ontake Ropuei
sights.description: Ropeway between Ontake's fifth and seventh stations, with a 2,150 m observation deck; the 2022 season ran from 25 June to 7 November.

sights.name: Kaido Roman On Yado Tsutaya

sights.name: Matsuo Falls

sights.name: Aburagi Forest

sights.name: Hakusan Shrine

sights.name: Mitake General Ground

sights.name: Kisokoma Forest Park Tennis Courts

sights.name: Gyoza Yama no Shakunage
sights.description: Rhododendron viewing spot in Kitaaiki.

sights.name: Megusuri no Ki

sights.name: Aiki Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins in Kitaaiki.

sights.name: Choja Forest

food.description: Restaurant in front of Komachiya Station serving sauce katsudon and gomoku ankake ramen; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:00-22:00 (subject to change), closed Tuesdays.

food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Komagane.

stays.description: Japanese-style inn in Toyosato, Nozawaonsen, facing the Nagasaka gondola lift, with gender-separated baths that are not hot spring.

stays.name: Lodge Hahnenkamm
stays.description: Lodge in Toyosato, Nozawaonsen, with a room containing two single beds and one sofa bed.

stays.name: Nozawa Onsen Lodge Denbee
stays.description: Lodge in Toyosato, Nozawaonsen, with a milky hot-spring bath and a log-house family room for one group a day.

day_to_day.name: Obuse Haiueioashisu Roadside Station Oashisu Obuse
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Obuse Comprehensive Park, reached from both Joshinetsu Expressway directions and local roads, with dining, souvenirs, dog run, farm shop, museum, park and major Reiwa 8 renovation.

day_to_day.name: Obuse Sogo Information Center
day_to_day.description: Local public facility in Obuse.

day_to_day.name: Iwataro Sekiya Farm Chokubai Tokoro
day_to_day.description: Farm produce shop selling seasonal Obuse-grown fruit, vegetables and rice, with grapes, apples and Obuse chestnuts in autumn, fresh juice from seasonal fruit, and produce from new farmers.

day_to_day.name: Matsubaya Main Store
day_to_day.description: Founded in the Edo period and moved to Obuse in early Meiji, this brewery has over 200 years of history.

day_to_day.name: Tojuro Gallery
day_to_day.description: This gallery at Nakamachi intersection sells ceramics, ink paintings, and ukiyo-e New Year cards by Tsukioka Tojuro.

day_to_day.name: Shioya Sakurai
day_to_day.description: This original chestnut-sweet shop still sells confections loved for two hundred years.

day_to_day.name: Sanpuro
day_to_day.description: This Obusedo branch opposite the Hokusai Museum sells chestnut sweets and ice cream.

day_to_day.name: Kokuhei Miso Brewery
day_to_day.description: Near Obuse Station, this brewery offers many naturally fermented miso varieties.

activities.name: Ryoan Antique Ceramics Collection
activities.description: This private museum next to Obuse Junior High's main gate displays rare old Imari and antique ceramics.

food.name: CAFE SAKU G
food.description: Cafe in the Kurian Fumido main shop in Obuse serving sweets made with chestnut paste and local Obuse milk, including Kuma-san Yaki; open 9:30-17:00, to 16:30 from mid-November through March.

food.name: cafe & marche ichinii
food.description: Cafe in a renovated 100-year-old former photo studio serving an Obuse chestnut parfait and a monthly parfait; open 10:00-17:00, closed Tuesdays, pets allowed on the terrace.

food.name: First-floor cafe in Obuse
food.description: First-floor cafe, a second shop of KUTEN, serving mini tarts; open 10:00-17:00 (until 15:00 in winter), closed Wednesday.

food.name: COFFEE & JAZZ BUD Gyararii Kura
food.description: Coffee shop in a former grain storehouse in Obuse, where 1950s-60s hard-bop jazz plays through a vacuum-tube amplifier; open 12:00-17:00, closed Monday-Thursday, with irregular closures.

food.name: Marute Kohi Baisenjo
food.description: Shop selling coffee roasted in a 120-year-old storehouse, with roasting experiences and takeout available, open 10:00-16:30 and closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Kanmi Kissa Sanada-tei
food.description: Sweets cafe serving a set of fukusa sushi, seasonal inari rolls and kudzu buns, plus chestnut kudzu with fruit and a drink; open 11:00-15:00 with no closing day.

food.name: ICHI cafe
food.description: Cafe serving coffee and sandwiches, including takeout, open 10:30-16:00 and closed on Wednesdays, Thursdays and irregular holidays.

food.name: cafe' + Delight
food.description: Cafe serving lunch-to-evening European dishes, including raclette-cheese baked curry, and summer shaved ice from 14:00-16:00; lunch 11:30-14:30, dinner 18:00-21:00, closed Thursday and irregular days.

food.name: KUTEN。 fuit&cake
food.description: Cafe serving seasonal tarts made with fruit from within 30 km of Obuse and a weekly seasonal lunch, with nationwide frozen-tart shipping, cafe hours 11:00-16:30, lunch until 14:30 and closed Mondays (may vary in winter).

food.name: Chuka-sai Daidai
food.description: Chinese restaurant serving its own dishes with Sichuan and Shanghai influences, with in-house doubanjiang, fermented black-bean sauce and chili oil, open for lunch 11:30-14:00 and dinner 17:30-22:00 and closed Tuesdays.

food.name: BEL ASIA FOOD
food.description: Asian restaurant whose owner is Thai, serving ethnic cuisine; lunch 11:00-15:00, dinner 17:00-21:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Chinese or Asian restaurant in Obuse
food.description: Dried-flower and pho shop serving Vietnamese pho, brothless pho and a weekly rice menu; open 11:30-16:00 (last order 15:30; from 12:30 on flower-class days), closed Sundays and Thursdays.

food.name: OBUSE Hanaya
food.description: Western restaurant on the Floral Garden grounds serving Obuse-grown vegetables; lunch 11:00-14:00, tea time 11:00-15:00, dinner 18:00-20:30 (last order 20:00); closed Thursdays and for Sunday and Wednesday dinner.

food.name: evolve
food.description: Italian restaurant serving lunch and dinner with local ingredients; the cafe menu includes Suzaku Monte Bianco, open 11:00-14:00 and 18:00-19:30, closed Wednesdays and twice monthly.

food.name: Jimono-ya Hibiki
food.description: Restaurant serving Obuse Kura Curry and draft local beer; open 11:30-14:30 and 17:30-21:00, closed Sunday evenings and Mondays.

food.name: Yoshoku Aoi
food.description: Restaurant in a renovated cocoon storehouse serving omurice, mixed fry and chestnut bavarois; lunch 11:00-14:00, cafe 11:00-16:00, dinner by reservation, closed Wednesday and Thursday.

food.name: Pace Italian Restaurant
food.description: Italian restaurant serving margherita, capricciosa and other seasonal-vegetable dishes; lunch 11:30-14:00 with handmade desserts, dinner 17:30-20:30 with wine pairings; closed Mondays and the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.

food.name: Soba Udon Kobiki
food.description: Soba and udon shop using Shinshu flour that also runs as an evening izakaya, with aimori (both noodles) and sansai takikomi gohan; lunch 11:00-15:00 in busy season only, izakaya 18:00-22:30, closed Thursday.

food.name: Donabe Ramen Takesan
food.description: Ramen shop serving donabe ramen, including Shinshu miso ramen made with miso from a nearby miso shop; open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-21:00, closed Thursday and Tuesday night.

food.name: Obuse Chuka Soba Takano
food.description: Chuka soba shop serving light chicken-broth ramen with homemade noodles and mabushi rice; lunch 11:00-14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner by reservation, closed Mondays.

food.name: Ichiryu Manpei
food.description: Restaurant with a lunch buffet of about 20 vegetable dishes made in the kitchen from its own farm and local farms; open 11:30-15:00, closed Wednesday.

food.name: Obuse Yori Tsuki Cuisine Kurabe Main Store
Katsuratei
food.description: Serves skewers, soba, and Kansai-style udon, with a kushiage-and-noodle lunch set and chestnut rice in autumn; lunch 11:30-14:30, dinner 17:30-21:00 last order, closed Monday and Tuesday, Sunday lunch irregular.

food.name: Yakushi Tofu Mameya
food.description: Tofu restaurant beside Yakushido serving tofu steak and tofu cutlet made with domestic soybeans and natural nigari, open 11:30-14:30 and 18:00-21:00 (evenings by reservation) and closed Wednesdays and Thursday evenings.

food.name: Wajiki Ryori Atobe
food.description: Japanese restaurant serving set meals, seafood, sushi, Shinshu mochi pork and Shinshu beef, with sake and wine; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:30, closed Thursdays.

food.name: Obuse-an
food.description: Shop serving soft-serve ice cream and hand-baked senbei made in its factory, including marron glace and miso soft serve, open 10:00-15:00 (hours vary by season) and closed on 31 December and 1 January.

food.name: Cake shop in Obuse
food.description: French confectionery shop serving cakes, pastries and baked sweets, including a white mont blanc and seasonal sweets; weekdays 11:00-18:00, weekends and holidays 11:00-17:00, closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

food.description: Confectionery shop and tea room selling Western sweets made with Obusedo chestnut paste, butter and fresh cream, with tea service 10:00-16:00, takeout 10:00-17:00 and no regular closing day.

food.name: Yogashiten Marunitsuta
food.description: Confectionery shop serving cakes made with peaches, apples and grapes from its own farm, with tatami seating facing a Japanese garden; open 11:00-17:00, closed Sunday to Thursday.

sights.name: Shingonshu Toyoyama Ha Joko Tera
sights.description: Shingon temple at the foot of Mount Karita, locally called Karita no Yakushi, whose thatched hip-and-gable Yakushi Hall of 1408 is a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Ko Dai Shrine
sights.description: Shrine derived from Ise Jingu and jointly enshrining Konpira, Yasaka, and Nishinomiya shrines; Yasuichi market is held in the grounds on January 14-15, with an Issa haiku stone.

sights.name: Obuse Museum Nakajima Chinami Kan
sights.description: Art museum with works by painter Nakajima Chinami and metal sculptor Haruyama Fuminori, a festival-float storehouse, exhibitions, a shop, and a cafe.

sights.name: Chikufu Do Main Shop
sights.description: Shop whose present building was opened in 1988, with an elevator and multipurpose toilets, and the Museum of Japanese Light and Nakano Clay Hina Hall on the grounds.

sights.name: Orai /ourai
sights.description: Complex combining a guesthouse, a work lounge, and dining serving Chinese food, cafe items, and sweets.

sights.name: Obuse Ranch milgreen
sights.description: Gelato shop in the Thousand-Year Forest serving gelato and cheese made with milk from ranch-raised Jersey cows, with views of the forest and calves.

sights.name: Shakaifukushi Hojin Kuri no Mi Sono
sights.description: Farm stand where service users organically farm and keep about 2,000 free-range chickens on fermented feed and seasonal wild grasses, selling eggs, seasonal vegetables, miso, and sweets.

stays.name: Masu Ichi Kyakuden
stays.description: Lodging in Obuse.

stays.name: Guesthouse in Obuse
stays.description: Guesthouse in central Obuse, converted from a storehouse that Hokusai saw.

stays.description: Inn at Obuse Onsen in Ganta, Obuse.

day_to_day.description: Viewing sessions are held mainly for overnight guests, using a 60-centimeter telescope.

activities.name: Yu no Sawa Onsen Ogawamura Baths
activities.description: Cold mineral spring baths with weakly alkaline sulfur water; adults 300 yen, children 100 yen, beside an indoor gateball court.

sights.description: Cherry blossom viewing spot in Ogawamura.

sights.name: Iizuna Yama
sights.description: Mountain with a one-way 50-minute trekking course from a highland area, with gazebos and observation decks along the path.

sights.name: Kiriyama no Autumn Leaves
sights.description: Autumn leaves viewing spot in Ogawamura.

sights.name: Oneyama no Sugi no Taiboku
sights.description: Large cedar tree in Ogawamura.

sights.name: O Ha Tsuki Icho
sights.description: Ginkgo that bears seeds with leaves attached only at tips of short fruiting spurs arising at about two-thirds or more of the trunk length.

sights.name: Kamikita O no Fufu Matsu
sights.description: Couple pine trees in Ogawamura.

sights.name: Obora Pond
sights.description: This nature-surrounded pond offers leisurely fishing, stocked by a local club, though angling is sometimes impossible.

sights.name: Shiraji Giant Horse Chestnut
sights.description: This giant tree has an eye-level girth of 4.5 meters and stands 40 meters tall.

sights.name: Alps Viewpoint Plaza (Kozenji Temple)
sights.description: At dusk the Northern Alps become silhouettes, wrapping viewers in an orange world.

sights.name: Hoshuzan Kozenji Temple
sights.description: This rare seven-hall temple complex in the prefecture is the final stop of the Shinano 33 Kannon pilgrimage.

sights.name: Furuyama Castle Ruins
sights.description: The original castle collapsed in 1787, and worship was moved to this former second bailey where a small shrine stands.

sights.name: Yakushi Cave
sights.description: This natural cave is where Edo ascetic Mokujiki Sankyo carved ten thousand Buddhas; a Yakushi image and stone Buddhas remain.

stays.name: Hoshi To Midori no Roman-kan
stays.description: Hoshi To Midori no Roman-kan is an inn at 1,000 m elevation in Inagaoka, Ogawa Village, Kamiminochi District.

day_to_day.name: Okaya Hot Spring Beautiful-Skin Bath Romanet
day_to_day.description: A hot-spring facility using Okaya Onsen by Lake Suwa, with a German-style bade pool, Roman bath, and sauna.

activities.name: Okaya Taiko
activities.description: At the Okaya Taiko Festival, 300 drummers play together on a 60-meter outdoor stage before visitors from across Japan.

activities.name: Tsurumine Park
activities.description: Central Japan's top azalea spot, with 30-plus varieties and 30,000 bushes peaking mid-to-late May, plus a festival.

activities.name: Okaya Silk Workshop
activities.description: Weaving and dyeing experiences (reservation required) in Okaya, once Japan's top silk town, plus a necktie sales corner.

activities.name: Okaya Hot Springs
activities.description: Hot springs beside Lake Suwa; bathe at Romanet's Roman bath, lodging facilities, or the hot-spring stand.

food.name: Cafe Hill Valley
food.description: Cafe serving coffee for 450 yen, tea for 400 yen, cake for 800 yen and sandwiches for 600 yen; open 10:00-22:00, closed irregularly.

food.name: Suwa Mizumi Service Area Outbound Restaurant Mizumi Sai
Inakaya
food.description: Restaurant serving eel, ayu, mountain vegetables, mushrooms, seasonal fish, horse sashimi and beef hoba-yaki; open 17:00-23:00 (last order 22:00), closed Sundays except holidays.

food.name: Ouna Komatsuya
food.description: Eel restaurant open 11:00-14:15 and 17:00-20:15, closing when the eel runs out; closed Tuesdays, or the next day if Tuesday is a holiday.

food.name: Taiyo Pan Chuodo Suwako Service Area (Kudari)
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Okaya.

food.name: Suwa Noyatsu Tokoro
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Okaya.

food.name: Fuji Ice Cream Okaya
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Okaya.

sights.name: Tsurumine Park no Tsutsuji
sights.description: Park azaleas begun in the early Showa era, when three freight-car loads arrived by mistake instead of 300 plants; about 30,000 plants of over 30 kinds bloom red, white, pink, and purple.

sights.name: Shutsu So Park no Katakuri
sights.description: Dogtooth violet viewing spot in Okaya.

sights.name: Kosaka Kannon In (Kosaka Park) no Ajisai
sights.description: Hydrangea planting of 800 plants in full bloom in mid-July after the rainy season, in blue, white, and purple, with a view of Lake Suwa.

sights.name: Yokogawa Kawa no Sakura Achi
sights.description: Cherry-blossom arch of about 400 trees, mainly Somei-yoshino, extending about 4 km along both embankments of the Yokogawa River.

sights.name: Former Watanabe Family Residence
sights.description: Birthplace of Shinshu's first minister, Kunitake, and sons Chiaki and Chifuyu; called the origin of modern houses. Prefectural treasure.

sights.name: Ilf Children's Art Museum
sights.description: Features Takei Takeo, who coined doga, and permanent works by Maurice Sendak of Where the Wild Things Are.

sights.name: Toriidaira Yamabiko Park
sights.description: A vast, scenic, nature-rich park on a 1,000-meter rise overlooking Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, and the Alps.

sights.name: Okaya Lakeside Park
sights.description: A Lake Suwa fountain rises 55 meters and is lit at night; cherry rows bloom fully in spring.

sights.name: Okaya Civic General Gymnasium
sights.description: A popular civic gymnasium for health promotion and a venue for various sports tournaments.

sights.name: Suwa Lakehill Country Club
sights.description: Its wooded course, rated 71.1, stirs challenge from average golfers to low-handicap players.

sights.name: Autumn Foliage at Izuhaya Park
sights.description: Peak late October to mid-November; many species yield shifting red, yellow, and orange leaves, also known for spring dogtooth violets.

sights.name: Takabocchi Plateau and Mount Hachibuse
sights.description: Refreshing plateau overlooking Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, Mount Fuji, and the Alps; azaleas bloom in June, daylilies in July.

sights.name: Swans of Lake Suwa
sights.description: Swans, a winter symbol since two whooper swans in 1974, now exceed 200 yearly, viewable against Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Prefectural Izuhaya Park
sights.description: Shrine grove is a city natural monument; 240 species color autumn, and the maple festival lights the park at night.

sights.name: Enrei Onodachi Park Lookout
sights.description: Famous for autumn leaves and birdsong in Japan's 100 Soundscapes; the only view of Yatsugatake, Fuji, and the Northern Alps.

sights.name: Kosaka Kannon-in Temple
sights.description: Rebuilt in 1715 by fourth Takashima lord Tadataka; Okuma-style work by Ushiyama Zensuke and Hanaoka Isoemon.

sights.name: Nashikubo Ruins
sights.description: A typical mountain settlement ruin on an alluvial fan overlooking Mount Fuji, where Nashikubo-style pottery was found.

sights.name: Former Hayashi Family Residence
sights.description: Silk-reeling family's mansion from the industry's peak, with an adjoining tearoom and Western house wrapped in gold leather paper.

sights.name: Dehaya Park
sights.description: Vast dogtooth-violet colonies delight visitors in mid to late April, and autumn foliage in late October to early November.

sights.name: Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: Panoramic views of Lake Suwa, Yatsugatake, Mount Fuji, and the Northern Alps; also known for sunrise and sunset.

sights.name: Okaya City Yamabiko International Skating Center
sights.description: A comprehensive sports facility where elite athletes train and beginners and the public can casually enjoy skating.

sights.name: Yamabiko Skate Forest Ice Arena
sights.description: Beside Yamabiko Park, families skate and curl even in summer on Japan's top-class ice, except mid-July through September.

sights.name: Enrei Outdoor Activity Center
sights.description: Adjacent to scenic Enrei Goryotachi Park, with a green sports house, campsite, lawn, field athletics, and running course.

sights.name: Wild Birds of Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: Every Sunday in May and June a bird bus runs; the beautiful songs and scenery rank among Japan's 100 Soundscapes.

sights.name: Autumn Foliage at Enrei Goryotachi Park
sights.description: A nature park around Shiojiri Pass, designated a prefectural bird forest, offering birdsong and autumn foliage worth seeing.

stays.name: Hotel in Hon, Okaya
stays.description: Hotel in Hon, Okaya with parking; 5-minute drive from Ryochushajo32Daiari!Okaya IC.

stays.name: Hotel in Chuo, Okaya
stays.description: Hotel in Chuo, Okaya with business travelers; 5-minute walk from Jrokaya Station.

stays.name: Hotel in Okaya
stays.description: Okaya Sentoraru Hotel Okaya Ekimae (BBH Hotel Gurupu) has 21-square-meter rooms with air purifiers, washlets, and air conditioning in Honmachi, Okaya.

stays.name: Guesthouse accommodation in Okaya
stays.description: Guesthouse accommodation in Okaya, bookable on Jalan.

day_to_day.name: Okuwa Roadside Station (Kirakusha)
day_to_day.description: Restaurants include Gurumeria Kiraku, Komekko Okuwa, and a snack corner; Shinshu salmon, Kiso beef, and soba are recommended.

activities.name: Atera Keikoku Campground
activities.description: Campground in Atera National Forest by the gorge, where the spring Bigansui, selected as a Shinshu noted water, flows out.

activities.name: Nozokido Forest Park Campground
activities.description: Highland campground at 1,000 meters offering tents to equipped cabins, trout fishing, barbecues, and starry nights.

food.name: Taiwan Cuisine Banri Kaori
food.description: Chinese or Asian restaurant in Okuwa.

sights.name: Ina Kawa Damu Ue Tozanguchi
sights.description: Trailhead above Inagawa Dam: vehicles cannot go past the lower gate, a hike-registration post stands nearby, and there is no parking, so hikers are asked to use taxis or similar.

sights.name: no Zokido Forest Park
sights.description: Forest park with Central Alps views, spring azaleas, blueberry picking from summer into autumn, a campground, and star viewing; open late April-late May and mid-July-late September.

sights.name: Atera Gorge
sights.description: Gorge with high-transparency water called Atera Blue that appears blue or green with the light, plus hinoki forest and steep rocks; private cars cannot enter in the restriction period.

sights.name: Suhara Yado no Mizu Fune
sights.description: Water troughs hollowed from sawara logs, used since the post-town era for washing rice, vegetables, and dishes and as a resting place.

sights.name: Atera Gorge no Mizu
sights.description: Gorge of emerald-green Atera Blue water with seasonal flowers, autumn foliage, a suspension bridge, and fences reused from old forest-railway rails; vehicle entry is restricted in summer.

sights.name: Hakusan Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 1344 with four national Important Cultural Property halls, Zao, Hakusan, Izu and Kumano, in plain one-bay nagare-zukuri, open only during festivals.

sights.name: Sadakatsu Tera
sights.description: Rinzai Myoshinji-school temple, the oldest of Kiso's three major temples, with nightingale-floor corridors, a garden, spring weeping cherries, and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Okuwa Folk History Museum
sights.description: Museum displaying forest-resident life and Nakasendo history of Suhara-juku and Nojiri-juku, plus a Nagano Prefecture treasure, perforated flanged pottery with a human face, nicknamed Eternal Smile.

sights.name: Okuwa Tami Gym
sights.description: Gym with two volleyball courts, two basketball courts, a judo-kendo room and changing rooms; classes are held regularly, and camp use with the adjacent sports park needs a reservation.

sights.name: Koiji Pass
sights.description: A corruption of Koji Pass whose forked red pine shelters welcoming Enmei Jizo; the overlook was Shinshu-certified in 2018.

sights.name: Nozokido Forest Park Azalea Garden
sights.description: Colonies of three-leaf and mountain azaleas fill the park, purple in late April and red from early to mid-May.

sights.name: Weeping Cherries at Joshoji Temple
sights.description: Joshoji, an Important Cultural Property and Kisoji's oldest historic temple, has a little-Kyoto garden, beautiful weeping cherries, and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Shinshu Famous and Secret Waters: Atera Gorge Beautiful Face Water
sights.description: Drinkable spring from Atera Gorge forest rocks; legend says an Owari official's wife grew fair washing her face with it.

stays.name: Inn in Okuwa
stays.description: Inn at Atera Onsen in Nojiri, Okuwa with riverside setting and scenic views.

day_to_day.name: Omachi City Tourism Association Station Information Office
day_to_day.description: This station information office offers bicycle rentals and guided tours.

day_to_day.name: Iizura Omachi Local Products Hall
day_to_day.description: Five minutes from JR Shinano-Omachi Station, this storehouse sells specialties and serves coffee and oyaki.

day_to_day.name: Omachi Dam Information Center
day_to_day.description: Panels and computers explain this multipurpose dam's flood control, water use, and surrounding nature.

day_to_day.name: Usausa Petit Farm
day_to_day.description: Wine workshop and farm guesthouse founded in 2010, growing cool-climate grapes in Omachi and Ikeda.

activities.name: Jigatake Ski Area

activities.name: Lake Kizaki Modern Boat
activities.description: Offers varied Lake Kizaki fishing boats plus SUP, wakeboarding, water skiing, and dog-friendly plans.

food.name: Café in Omachishi
food.description: Cafe with large windows overlooking the Northern Alps; open 10:00-17:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Tawara-ya Meshi
food.description: Chinese or Asian restaurant in Omachishi.

food.name: Yamashina

food.name: Ganso Teuchi Soba Furuyaso
